title: Your First AI Experiment knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Your First AI Experiment”?
options: Your First AI Experiment focuses on Selecting a simple AI task; Providing an input; Observing the output. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. AI literacy begins with the task and the people affected by it. Treat an AI output as a proposal...
It guarantees correct outcomes in every context and removes the need for independent evaluation.
It is always identical to a fixed if/then script, regardless of the data or task.
It can be trusted solely because its output is fluent or its internal score is high.
questions.answer_key: Your First AI Experiment focuses on Selecting a simple AI task; Providing an input; Observing the output. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. AI literacy begins with the task and the people affected by it. Treat an AI output as a proposal...
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the topic this way: Your First AI Experiment focuses on Selecting a simple AI task; Providing an input; Observing the output. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. AI literacy begins with the task and the people affected by it. Treat an AI output as a proposal... The distractors claim guarantees or equivalences that are not supported by the curriculum.

questions.prompt: When applying “Your First AI Experiment” to a new problem, which practice is the strongest default?
options: Skip evaluation when the first demonstration looks convincing.
Define the goal and boundaries, test realistic cases, and inspect failure modes before relying on the result.
Tune all decisions directly on the final test examples until the score improves.
Assume a method that worked once will work on every population and input distribution.
questions.answer_key: Define the goal and boundaries, test realistic cases, and inspect failure modes before relying on the result.
questions.explanation: Define the goal and boundaries, test realistic cases, and inspect failure modes before relying on the result. This practice makes assumptions visible and gives a reviewer evidence beyond one convincing demonstration.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is appropriately cautious after a system demonstrates “Your First AI Experiment”?
options: The system has proven its result is unbiased and safe for every use.
A successful example removes the need for monitoring or documentation.
No. Check uncertainty, context, data quality, security, and affected users; report limitations and use human oversight appropriate to the impact.
Any numeric score or generated explanation is a guarantee of factual correctness.
questions.answer_key: No. Check uncertainty, context, data quality, security, and affected users; report limitations and use human oversight appropriate to the impact.
questions.explanation: Observed performance is conditional on the test conditions. Review uncertainty, context, risks, and failures before deciding how the system may be used.
